cards.name: and_ancilla_ccz_lowering_with_measured_uncompute
cards.identity:
Lower every ccz/ccx on the Toffoli level through a temporary logical-AND ancilla, and share one AND across a run of ccz gates with the same control pair.

(1) AND-compute gadget A(x,y -> a), 4 T gates, one CLEAN ancilla a in |0>: the standard 4-T 'temporary AND' / 'Toffoli with measurement-free compute' construction (Jones 2013 Fig. 1, Gidney 2018 Fig. 4): H(a); T(x); T(y); T(a); CX(x,a); CX(y,a); CX(a,x); CX(a,y); Tdg(x); Tdg(y); CX(a,x); CX(a,y); H(a); S(a) -- i.e. a Clifford skeleton of CNOTs/H/S carrying exactly 4 pi/4 rotations, with the net action |x>|y>|0> -> |x>|y>|x AND y> exactly (no relative phase, controls untouched). Any equivalent 4-T AND skeleton may be substituted as long as the judge certifies the map on all 4 control values.

(2) Use: ccz(x,y,z) becomes A(x,y->a); CZ(a,z); A^-1. ccx(x,y,z) becomes A(x,y->a); CX(a,z); A^-1. Because the AND wire holds the classical value x AND y, CZ(a,z) applies exactly the phase (-1)^{x y z}.

(3) Measured uncompute A^-1 (0 T): H(a); MEASURE(a) -> bit m; if m == 1 apply CZ(x,y); reset/retire a. Zero T gates, zero rotations.

(4) AND SHARING (where the gain over 4T-per-Toffoli comes from): take a maximal run of consecutive gates g_1..g_k in the op list that are all ccz (or ccx) sharing the SAME unordered control pair {x,y}, such that between g_1 and g_k no op in the segment writes to x or y (no x/h/cx-target/ccx-target/measure on x or y; diagonal gates z/s/t/cz/rz on x or y are permitted since they commute with the AND value, as are arbitrary ops on the distinct targets z_1..z_k). Emit ONE A(x,y->a), then CZ(a,z_i) (resp. CX(a,z_i)) in place of each g_i, then ONE measured uncompute after g_k. Ancillas are allocated from a free pool and reused after uncompute, so at most the peak number of simultaneously live ANDs is added to the qubit count.
cards.correctness:
Relaxed contract: clean ancillas start and end in |0> and every measurement branch is checked for phase consistency.

AND gadget: the 4-T construction is a known exact implementation of the map |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y> (it is the Toffoli-with-one-ancilla-free 'AND' of Jones/Gidney, obtained from the 7-T Toffoli by discarding the uncompute half). Its correctness is a finite check over the 4 computational control values plus linearity, which the judge verifies exactly over Z[omega] since all gates are Clifford+T.

Target action: once a holds the classical bit x&y, CZ(a,z) multiplies |x,y,z> by (-1)^{(x&y) z} = (-1)^{xyz}, which is exactly ccz(x,y,z); CX(a,z) flips z iff x&y, exactly ccx(x,y,z). The controls x,y are computational-basis-preserved by the construction, so the AND value is a genuine classical copy and no entanglement with a survives after step (3).

Measured uncompute: the state before uncompute is sum_x alpha_x |x,y>|x&y>. Measuring a in the X basis gives outcome m with probability 1/2 and leaves sum_x alpha_x (-1)^{m (x&y)} |x,y>, i.e. the original state acted on by CZ(x,y)^m. Applying CZ(x,y) classically conditioned on m restores the state exactly, with branch coefficient c_m = 1/sqrt(2) identical for every input x (phase consistency holds), and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. No T gate appears: H, measure, and a classically controlled CZ are all Clifford.

AND sharing: a&b is a classical function of the control wires only. If no op between g_1 and g_k modifies the computational value of x or y, the stored bit remains x&y throughout, so each CZ(a,z_i) is still exactly ccz(x,y,z_i). Diagonal ops on x,y commute with the |x>,|y> basis labels and therefore cannot change x&y; they commute past a as well since a is only touched by CNOTs controlled on x,y inside the gadget, which are already finished. Hence the single compute/uncompute pair is sound for the whole run.
cards.trigger: IRCircuit (Toffoli level). Scan the gate list left to right. For each unvisited ccz or ccx gate g at index i with controls {x,y} and target z: greedily extend to the maximal j >= i such that every ccz/ccx in indices [i..j] that is included has control set exactly {x,y}, and no gate in [i..j] applies a non-diagonal operation to x or y (forbidden on x or y: x, h, cx as target, ccx as target, measure, classically controlled non-diagonal; allowed: z, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz, cz, and the control slots of cx/ccx/ccz, plus any gate acting only on other wires). Emit a match {controls: (x,y), members: [indices], span: (i,j)}. Matches are disjoint by construction. On adder_8 all 57 ccz gates are matched; the trigram histogram (ccz ccz ccz: 20, ccz ccz h: 12, h ccz ccz: 11) shows long adjacent ccz runs, so many matches contain 2 or 3 members sharing a carry control pair. Singleton matches (run length 1) are still emitted: they already pay 4 T instead of 7.
cards.expected_effect: Each match costs exactly 4 T total, independent of how many ccz gates it covers; all 7-T Toffoli decompositions disappear. adder_8 has 57 ccz = 399 T today. With ~39 maximal control-pair runs over those 57 gates (the ccz-ccz adjacency counts above), the lowered circuit costs ~39 * 4 = ~156 T, plus zero T from the measured uncomputes. Added Clifford traffic: ~8-12 CX per match and one H + one measurement + one classically controlled CZ per match. Qubits grow by the peak number of simultaneously live AND ancillas; with pool reuse this is small (a ripple-carry structure keeps 1-2 live at a time), so ~24 -> 25 or 26. Even the pessimistic no-sharing case (57 singleton matches) gives 57 * 4 = 228 T, i.e. a guaranteed >= 171 T saving, and beats pyzx (173) and TKET (361) in the shared case.
cards.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2:74 (2018) (temporary logical-AND, measurement-based uncompute); N. C. Jones, 'Novel constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate', PRA 87, 022328 (2013) (4-T AND / Toffoli with ancilla and classical fix-up).

cards.name: shared_and_value_cache_by_anf_matching
cards.identity:
Globally cache AND values by symbolic wire-value matching, so that one 4-T temporary-AND ancilla serves every ccz/ccx in the circuit whose control pair carries the SAME pair of logical values, no matter how far apart they are and no matter how the control wires are overwritten in between.

(1) Symbolic pass. Give each of the n input wires a free GF(2) variable. Sweep the gate list and keep, for every wire, its current value as an algebraic normal form (ANF) polynomial over those variables (a set of monomials, canonicalized and sorted; cap the monomial count, e.g. 64, and mark a wire UNKNOWN on overflow):
   x(q):      v[q] <- v[q] + 1
   cx(c,t):   v[t] <- v[t] + v[c]
   ccx(a,b,t):v[t] <- v[t] + v[a]*v[b]   (polynomial product, reduced by u^2 = u)
   z/s/sdg/t/tdg/cz/ccz/rz: diagonal, v unchanged
   h(q):      v[q] <- UNKNOWN (and any later gate with an UNKNOWN control is skipped by this rule)
   measure / classically controlled gates: v[target] <- UNKNOWN

(2) Product key. For each ccz/ccx gate g at index i with controls {c1,c2} (target z), if v[c1] and v[c2] are both known, its key is the unordered pair K(g) = {v[c1], v[c2]} of ANF polynomials -- the logical bit the gate needs is the product of those two polynomials. Group all ccz/ccx gates by key. A group with occurrences i_1 < ... < i_k (k >= 1) is one match.

(3) Emission for a match with key {p,q} and occurrences i_1..i_k. At i_1, before the gate, allocate one CLEAN ancilla a in |0> and emit the 4-T temporary-AND compute A(c1,c2 -> a) on the wires that currently hold p and q (|p,q,0> -> |p,q,p&q|, controls untouched, exactly 4 pi/4 rotations in a Clifford skeleton of H/S/CX). Replace each occurrence i_j by cz(a, z_j) if g_{i_j} is ccz, or cx(a, z_j) if it is ccx (the target wire of each occurrence is whatever that gate's own target was; targets may differ between occurrences and may be rewritten in between -- irrelevant). After the last occurrence i_k, emit the 0-T measured uncompute: h(a); measure(a) -> m; classically controlled cz on the two wires that hold p and q at that point (the controls of g_{i_k}); retire a to the free pool.

(4) Ancilla pool. Live intervals [i_1, i_k] of different matches may overlap; allocate from a pool and reuse, so the qubit count grows by the peak number of simultaneously live cached AND bits.

Cost: 4 T per DISTINCT key, instead of the current book's 4 T per maximal ADJACENT same-control-pair run.
cards.correctness:
Relaxed contract: the added ancillas start and end in |0>, and every measurement branch is checked for function + phase consistency by the judge.

(a) The ANF sweep is exact bookkeeping. On the computational basis the gates x, cx, ccx act as the stated affine/quadratic updates on wire values, and over GF(2) with u^2 = u the ANF of each wire value is the unique multilinear polynomial representing it. Diagonal gates (z, s, t, rz, cz, ccz) do not change any computational-basis label, so they cannot change any v[q]. h and measurement destroy the label, which is why the affected wire becomes UNKNOWN and no key may reference it. Hence, for every gate the rule touches, v[c1] and v[c2] are provably the exact logical values on its control wires at that point in the circuit, for every input.

(b) Value, not wire, is what the gadget needs. ccz(c1,c2,z) applies the phase (-1)^{v[c1] v[c2] v[z]} and ccx(c1,c2,z) flips z iff v[c1] v[c2] = 1. Both depend on the control wires only through the single classical bit b = v[c1]&v[c2]. If a holds b, then cz(a,z) applies (-1)^{b v[z]} and cx(a,z) flips z iff b = 1, i.e. exactly the original gate.

(c) The cached bit stays valid across arbitrary distance. This is the whole point and the fix to the earlier limitation. The ancilla a is written only by its own compute gadget and is not an operand of any other emitted gate until its uncompute, so its stored bit is frozen at the value b = p&q computed at i_1. At a later occurrence i_j the required bit is v[c1']&v[c2'] where {v[c1'], v[c2']} = {p, q} by construction of the key -- equality of ANF polynomials means equality of the represented Boolean functions, hence of the bit, on every input. The control WIRES may have been overwritten, moved, or recomputed in between (exactly what happens in a carry chain and in its compute/uncompute mirror); only the logical values must match, and they do. No condition on intervening gates is needed at all, beyond the UNKNOWN rule of (a).

(d) Measured uncompute, 0 T. Before uncompute the state is sum_x alpha_x |psi_x>|p(x)&q(x)>. Measuring a in the X basis gives m in {0,1} with probability 1/2 and leaves sum_x alpha_x (-1)^{m p(x) q(x)} |psi_x>, i.e. the state acted on by the diagonal map (-1)^{m p q}. At index i_k the wires c1,c2 of g_{i_k} hold p and q, so the classically controlled cz(c1,c2) applied iff m = 1 cancels that phase exactly. The branch coefficient is c_m = 1/sqrt(2), the same for every input x (phase consistency), and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. H, measurement and a classically controlled CZ contain no T gate, so uncompute is free. The ancilla is returned in a computational basis state and is reset to |0> before reuse.

(e) Groups are independent: distinct keys use distinct ancillas, each ancilla's compute and uncompute bracket its own occurrences, and the gadgets commute with everything outside their own operand sets in the basis-label sense used above.
cards.trigger: IRCircuit at Toffoli level (gate names in x z h s sdg t tdg cx cz ccx ccz, measure, classically controlled). Run the ANF sweep of step (1) over the whole gate list. Collect every ccz/ccx gate whose two control wires both have a known ANF at its position; key it by the canonicalized unordered pair of those ANFs. Emit one match per distinct key, carrying (key, ordered list of occurrence indices, per-occurrence target wire and gate type). Matches with k >= 2 occurrences are the profitable ones and are emitted first (sorted by k descending, then by first index) so the runner tries the biggest wins first; k = 1 matches are also emitted, since they already cost 4 T instead of 7. Gates with an UNKNOWN control, and gates whose ANF exceeds the monomial cap, are left untouched and fall back to the existing book rule. The rule rewrites the op list in one pass per match, inserting the compute gadget immediately before the first occurrence and the measured uncompute immediately after the last.
cards.expected_effect: adder_8 is 57 ccz on 24 qubits and currently sits at 216 T = 54 temporary-AND computes, because the accepted adjacency rule can only fuse ccz gates that are CONSECUTIVE and share the same control WIRES, and the recorded limitation is exactly that 'the carry controls change from gate to gate'. Under ANF keying, wires stop mattering: the adder's carry logic computes a small set of distinct carry/propagate products, and the circuit's compute half and its uncompute (garbage-clearing) half request the very same products a second time, so the same key reappears. Every repeated key collapses from 4 T per occurrence to 4 T total. With the compute/uncompute mirror alone pairing most of the 54 current AND computes, the distinct-key count should fall to roughly 24-30, i.e. about 96-120 T, versus 216 T now; even a partial collapse to 36 distinct keys gives 144 T. Gates removed: no Clifford target gates disappear, but about half of the 4-T AND computes do, each replaced by a free cz/cx on a still-live cached ancilla plus a free measured uncompute. Qubits grow by the peak number of simultaneously live cached ANDs; because an ancilla must stay live from the first to the last occurrence of its key, the mirror structure keeps several alive at once, so expect roughly 24 -> 30-34 qubits (T-count is the primary metric, qubits only the tiebreaker). The same mechanism should help mcx_10 (all ccz share a nested control structure) and modred_21.
cards.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2:74 (2018) (temporary logical-AND with measurement-based, T-free uncompute); C. H. Bennett, 'Logical reversibility of computation', IBM J. Res. Dev. 17, 525 (1973) (compute-copy-uncompute: the uncompute half re-requests the same intermediate values); M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits via matroid partitioning', IEEE TCAD 33, 1476 (2014) (tracking wire values as GF(2) polynomials / parity labels through CNOT-Toffoli networks); N. C. Jones, PRA 87, 022328 (2013) (4-T AND).

Measuring a in the X basis gives m in {0,1} with probability 1/2 and leaves sum_x alpha_x (-1)^{m p(x) q(x)} |psi_x>, i.e. the state acted on by the diagonal map (-1)^{m p q}. At index i_k the wires c1,c2 of g_{i_k} hold p and q, so the classically controlled cz(c1,c2) applied iff m = 1 cancels that phase exactly. The branch coefficient is c_m = 1/sqrt(2), the same for every input x (phase consistency), and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. H, measurement and a classically controlled CZ contain no T gate, so uncompute is free. The ancilla is returned in a computational basis state and is reset to |0> before reuse.

(e) Groups are independent: distinct keys use distinct ancillas, each ancilla's compute and uncompute bracket its own occurrences, and the gadgets commute with everything outside their own operand sets in the basis-label sense used above.
